author: Grace Velez
title: Simulation & Collaboration: GCSC molding future nurses - NewsBreak
text:
By Grace Velez ,
5 hours ago
BAY COUNTY, Fla. ( WMBB ) – Two of Bay County’s oldest and most important institutions are forming a new partnership that will be essential to the region’s future healthcare.
Gulf Coast State College nursing students will have their own simulation lab on campus in the future.
Until then, Ascension Sacred Heart Bay has opened up its labs so students can get real-world experiences as soon as possible.
“But being in this space really allows us to take the simulation to the next level,” Gulf Coast State College Nursing Division Chair Dr. Keri Matheus said.
Students will treat the simulation like a real patient, and it won’t be hard to imagine. The simulation can blink, its pupils react to light, and it can talk. It has every pulse a human has. It can scream, cough, and cry. Instructors can manipulate it to have uneven breath sounds, urinate, vomit, and several other symptoms.
“Inserting a catheter and it’ll give you like urine flashback, and then it has lung sounds, and it can show you the different lung sounds, the pulses, peripheral pulses. All of that is really neat,” Nursing Student Katie Rupprecht said.
Both students and health care professionals say they’re looking forward to making mistakes in this simulation setting. Mistakes are actually crucial learning opportunities.
“Making mistakes so I can be educated, and I don’t want to make them in the real world,” Nursing Student Kanon Smith said.
“I want to know that we are growing the nurses of tomorrow in this hospital. I want to make sure that they have the best training possible. So, this does set them up for success, putting them in these environments in these situations,” Clinical Professional Development Manager Meghan Upfold said.
Upfold says it’s a safe space where they can provide students with real-time feedback.
They’ll be able to see vitals up on the monitor, and they’ll be able to communicate with their instructors and fellow students throughout the simulation.
“If they have any questions, they’re able to speak to us. We can hear what’s going on, and we can give real-time feedback and say, hey, maybe the patient’s heart rate is going lower. What should you do now? What would be the next course of action afterwards?” Upfold explained.
Students are eager and appreciative of the opportunity.
“It’s amazing. And everyone’s been so welcoming. It’s just really important for us to have an opportunity like this and expand our knowledge,” Rupprecht said.
Having a simulation lab on campus in the future will be a huge win for the nursing program, but practicing in a hospital environment has its own advantages.
“I think I want to work in the E.R., but as far as being in a hospital has shown me that there are a thousand places a nurse can be,” said Smith.
Ascension Sacred Heart Bay nursing officials are hoping many of these students will someday work at the hospital.
“I like the Bay Area, I like where I’m at, and I want to I want to stay and work here,” added Smith.
